title: Henry Harden's band and the Rhythm Club on Jackson Avenue
summary: Harris recalls Harden's death and the Rhythm Club building, its two dance floors, and weekly radio broadcasts.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: what happened to Henry Harden the band you used to play big Henry Harden you used to play a tenor
Henry Harden Henry Harden died you see I was waiting on him at the rhythm club we used to broadcast on the rhythm club
The Rhythm Club was on Jackson Avenue in Durbanee.
I remember that. That was one of the swellest clubs they had at that time.
What happened? Is that building still there?
It's still there but it's all shaggy. They got room in where the dancers was and now they got room in the thing.
They got another club a couple blocks down. A fine club.
I remember that about 20 years ago almost since I remember singing.
The Rhythm Club one time they went up on the balcony and everything.
Oh yeah they had balcony. They danced downstairs and they danced upstairs.
Oh yeah. Yeah and the same band worked for both floors.

For both parts. See the balcony was facing the bandstand. See the music going upstairs and see the people that are keeping downstairs. Yeah we used to broadcast there a half hour every Sunday night. Around about 9 o'clock.
